### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54d6726c09019bd1d9da29b7aee3fb9e907dbb0a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `af3df1360ea4e4b0d4627b6907f4a9dc31c9696e` — the merge of head `9702f829713da041f4b5f499d92d8d45adcd72bb` into base `54d6726c09019bd1d9da29b7aee3fb9e907dbb0a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin af3df1360ea4e4b0d4627b6907f4a9dc31c9696e && git checkout af3df1360ea4e4b0d4627b6907f4a9dc31c9696e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 54d6726c09019bd1d9da29b7aee3fb9e907dbb0a 9702f829713da041f4b5f499d92d8d45adcd72bb && git checkout -B drift-repro 54d6726c09019bd1d9da29b7aee3fb9e907dbb0a && git merge --no-ff 9702f829713da041f4b5f499d92d8d45adcd72bb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54d6726c09019bd1d9da29b7aee3fb9e907dbb0a
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `81f84a9a7a5ade0f3b8bec86a6be6b95964ab49c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #37566 (body, claim, triage, os-dev-report), PR #37581 (body, 50-file list, net diff `origin/main...81f84a9a7a`), follow-up card #37618, and the check-runs on this head. Every concluded check-run is `success` or `skipped`, and none is failing or pending. Test Core 1–10/10, Test UI 1–16/16, Type Check UI, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates (incl. docs & code guards, PM dispatch-gates), Check Changeset, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate and Governed Surface Queue Guard all pass. I take those conclusions as the gate verdicts.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

- `@objectstack/platform-objects`: the exported `STUDIO_APP.label` value changes from `Studio` to `App Studio`, and `apps.studio.label` changes in all eleven translation packs (zh-CN 应用搭建, zh-Hant 應用搭建, the eight Latin packs plus en `App Studio`). **Right.** This is the ADR-0084 `#amendment-2026-11-26-position` ruling ("Its name is App Studio, and 应用搭建 in a Chinese interface… Only display text changes"). `STUDIO_APP.name` stays `studio`, and the new test pins that.
- `apps.studio.label` source hashes: all ten tables move `5aaaaea2294ee893` → `479a1bf587b5965e`. All ten carry the same digest, and that is correct because they all record the same `en` source. **Right, and it is load-bearing.** Every pack's value was re-translated in this change, so re-recording the digest is the sanctioned "update value AND digest" pair, not the forbidden "refresh digest alone". Without it, zh-CN and zh-Hant would be served the English source through `withSourceFallback`. The new `studio-display-name.test.ts` asserts the served label (after fallback) in every locale of `SetupAppTranslations`, and it is green in Test Core. That proves the digest matches without a local probe.
- `@object-ui/i18n` locale packs (all eleven): values of `console.studio.title`, `topbar.designInStudio`, `topbar.openAppInStudio`, `topbar.viewInStudio`, `layout.appSwitcher.editAppInStudio` and `layout.appSwitcher.openAppInStudio` change. No key is added, removed or renamed. **Right.**
- `@object-ui/i18n` studio namespace: the `engine.studio.mark` value changes (en `App Studio`, zh 应用搭建). This is the existing key `StudioBackToApp` renders in `data-testid="studio-mark"`, so there is no new key, and #37456 is pointed at it. **Right.**
- `@object-ui/app-shell` (private: `"private": true`, so it is not published and needs no changeset entry): three inline `defaultValue` literals in `AppHeader.tsx`, `AppSwitcher.tsx` and `SidebarAppMenu.tsx` change to equal the new `en` values. `check-i18n-call-site-keys` forces this. **Right.** These are string literals only, with no logic change.

**Seat Q1 (display-only).** Yes, only displayed strings move. I checked each forbidden class against the diff:

- Routes and URLs: none. `/studio/...` hrefs are still asserted unchanged, for example `AppSwitcher.appIdentity-12201` `href '/studio/com.acme.hotcrm/data'` and `SidebarAppMenu-36112` `'/studio/com.acme.crm/metadata/object/crm_lead'`.
- Metadata keys: none. `STUDIO_APP.name` is `studio`, and the new test pins it.
- i18n keys: none. Every hunk in the locale and namespace files is value-only, and the source-hash path `apps.studio.label` is unchanged.
- Object and API names: none.
- Test ids: none. `app-switcher-view-in-studio`, `app-switcher-edit-in-studio`, `studio-mark`, `studio-back`, `app-view-in-studio-button` and `sidebar-app-menu-view-in-studio` are unchanged.
- Stored values: none. The label is code-defined display metadata.

I found no consumer that matches `label === 'Studio'` or selects on the old door text, in source or in e2e/QA suites. The remaining `label: 'Studio'` test fixtures (`HomePage.desktopNoApps-36732`, `AppContent.*-12079/12113`, `UnifiedSidebar.studioNoHome-12113`, `useNavigationSync`, and console tests) are self-contained: each fixture supplies its own label and asserts against that, so none of them silently became vacuous.

**Seat Q2 (i18n).** Consistent. Every changed key changes in all eleven UI packs, with en and zh-Hans/zh-Hant in step:

- Chinese packs read 在应用搭建中… / 在應用搭建中….
- The Latin and CJK-with-Latin-name packs swap `Studio` for `App Studio` in place. Word order is kept in de (`im App Studio`), ja (`App Studio で`) and ko (`App Studio에서`).
- The ten platform-objects packs agree with en.
- The studio namespace ships only en and zh by ruling, so both are updated.

No hard-coded literal was introduced. The only literals added outside the packs are the three `t(key, { defaultValue })` call-site forms the gate accepts, plus comments.

**Seat Q4 (re-pointed pins).** They still pin something real, and one is tighter than before:

- `StudioDesignSurface.backToApp-36501` `studio-mark` went from a substring `toHaveTextContent('Studio')` (which `App Studio` would also have satisfied) to an anchored `/^App Studio$/`.
- The `studio-back` pins in `-36501`, `-11553` and `PackageFormDialog.newAppStep-36748` keep their full anchored `^Back to app·NAME·App Studio$` shape.
- The door pins in `AppHeader…-12615`, `AppSwitcher…-12201/-12605` and `SidebarAppMenu-36112` stay exact-text or anchored. The zh pin is exact equality on `在应用搭建中查看`, and `residue-namespaces-3546` keeps exact en and zh equality on `topbar.designInStudio`.
- The negative pins (`queryByText(...)` / `queryByRole(... name)` toBeNull in `SidebarAppMenu-36112` and `ShellPageActions-36111`) were correctly re-pointed to the new text. Leaving the old text there would have made them pass vacuously.
- `untranslated-identity-4376` changes only the reason string. The identity exemption for `console.studio.title` remains justified, because the Latin packs still equal en.

**Findings**

- **S1 (should-fix): the changeset names the wrong key for the brand.** `.changeset/37566-app-studio-display-name.md` says `console.studio.title` is "the Studio crumb, and the key the Studio brand reads". The brand (`studio-mark`) reads `engine.studio.mark`. That key is renamed here and is the one #37456 is told to reuse, but the changeset never names it. The changeset also omits the five door keys. This text becomes the published CHANGELOG of `@object-ui/i18n`, so a reader would point the brand at the wrong key. Fix: correct the sentence to name `engine.studio.mark` as the brand key and `console.studio.title` as the AppHeader crumb, and list the door keys.
- **N1 (nit): zh-Hant reads the brand in Simplified Chinese.** The studio namespace ships en and zh only, and `matchLanguageTag` serves `zh-Hant` from `zh`. A zh-Hant user therefore sees the brand as 应用搭建 (Simplified) beside the crumb and app label 應用搭建 (Traditional). Before this PR both read `Studio`, so the mismatch is new but small. The en+zh-only namespace is a standing ruling (objectstack#25922), so no change is owed here. It is worth one line on #37618 or the namespace's next card.

### ② Semver level

Changeset: `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`, `@object-ui/i18n: patch`. **Matches what the diff publishes.**

- The diff changes the values of an exported constant's display field and of translation strings.
- No export, type, key or schema is added or removed.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` is private and correctly absent.
- Check Changeset passes on this head.

`Clause-②: no` (PR body and changeset). **Right.** The diff adds no new declared capability or accept-set entry, and no published schema or governed path is touched.

**Seat Q3.** Yes, `Clause-②: no` at patch is right for both packages. The only by-value reads I found are:

- this PR's own tests;
- the generated `en`-source digest, which is re-recorded in the same change, so `withSourceFallback` serves each translation;
- the `check-i18n-call-site-keys` pairing, which is updated in the same change.

No repo consumer uses the app label as a lookup key: app lookup is by `name: 'studio'`, which is unchanged. No snapshot file captures the label. A downstream consumer that matched on the literal `'Studio'` label would be relying on display text, which the ADR ruling explicitly frees to change.

`Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's flags from the os-dev-report:

- **(1) Three app-shell layout sources outside the claimed file surface.** Accepted. The call-site-keys gate forces the `defaultValue` literal edits, which are string-only, and the claim's "label + locale text" intent covers them.
- **(2) Test-only edits in `studio-design/**` and `metadata-admin/**`.** Accepted. The claim forbids touching `studio-design/**` *components*. Only two test files there changed, with regex lines only, and no component was edited, so this does not collide with #37454 or #37456.
- **(3) PR body written before (1) and (2).** Resolved. The body on this head now lists the `SidebarAppMenu` `'View in Studio'` fallback and all three header-pin files.
- **Out-of-scope flake** (`designModeMenuSave-36363`, load or order dependent). Noted. Test UI is 16/16 green on this head, so nothing is owed here.

`open_questions[0]` (about 30 prose "Studio" strings per pack, plus `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`) is answered. Option A was taken: follow-up card #37618 is filed under #37424. It names `common.editInStudio`, `console.studio.accessRequired`, the Studio-namespace sentences, `console.ai.viewBuiltAppInStudio` and `empty.openInStudio`, and it is gated on this PR merging. Keeping the package manifest `name: 'Studio'` (`packages/apps/studio`) is correct: it is a package name, which the card's ⛔ list excludes.

**Seat Q5.** Nothing has to move into this PR. The card scoped the change to the label, the brand and page titles, and the remaining mixed-name surfaces are each tracked by #37618 or are nits:

- **N2 (nit): mixed names that #37618 already tracks.** A Chinese UI now shows these together:
  - the brand reads 应用搭建 while the `studio-back-to-app` button beside it has the tooltip `engine.studio.backToAppTitle` (离开 Studio，回到 {app} / "Leave Studio…");
  - other doors into Studio keep the old name: `common.editInStudio` (PageView pencil, 在 Studio 中编辑), `empty.openInStudio` and `console.ai.viewBuiltAppInStudio`, beside the renamed switcher and top-bar doors.

  The tooltip on the brand's own widget is the strongest candidate to have ridden along. #37618 covers all of these ("every prose mention", with the three door keys named), so no change is owed here.
- **N3 (nit): a user doc quotes renamed control text, and #37618 does not list it.** `content/docs/build-without-code.mdx:22` quotes the control as **"Design in Studio"**, but `topbar.designInStudio` now reads "Design in App Studio". #37618 lists only `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`. Fix: add this file to #37618's list, or fix the one line here.

SQL push-down (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 5): not applicable. The diff adds no data access, id materialisation or in-app join.

Security: none. The diff contains display strings only.
